groups.title: First-party extensions (coming soon)
groups.blurb: Official Caduceus extensions in development — same drag-in format as community extensions, maintained in-repo. They ship separately from built-ins so API keys, extra tools you install, and permissions stay explicit when you turn them on.

items.name: Google Translate
items.detail: Calls the Cloud Translation API with your key (billed per character). Coming as a first-party extension rather than a built-in that depends on an undocumented free endpoint.

items.name: Jira and Linear
items.detail: Issue search and quick actions over each product's API. Coming soon — you'll bring your own account; both products assume a paid team plan for real use.

items.name: Internet speed test
items.detail: Measure download/upload against an endpoint you choose. Coming as an extension so Caduceus does not silently consume someone else's bandwidth on your behalf.

items.name: Authy import
items.detail: Authy has no public API and desktop apps were discontinued in 2024. A first-party path is being explored with the same bar as any extension that touches 2FA material.

items.name: Starting a macOS Focus session
items.detail: macOS does not expose Focus directly; the supported route is a Shortcuts action. Coming as an extension that runs the Shortcut you configure.

items.name: Bluetooth device switching
items.detail: Connect a named Bluetooth device from the palette. Coming with an optional helper — macOS still has no supported public API for this.

items.name: Keyboard backlight control
items.detail: Adjust keyboard brightness where hardware allows. Coming as an extension; may require a helper because Apple provides no stable public API.

items.name: Per-application volume
items.detail: Set volume per app via CoreAudio. Coming as an extension — likely a separate helper or driver, not a single built-in command.

items.name: Downloading video from a website
items.detail: Wraps yt-dlp you install yourself. Coming soon — Caduceus will not bundle yt-dlp; site terms stay between you and the host.

items.name: Text expansion that types for you
items.detail: System-wide expansion needs a keyboard event tap and a dedicated opt-in. Coming as its own first-party extension after a focused security review — palette snippets stay the built-in alternative.

commandGroups.title: Window management
commandGroups.blurb: Snap, resize and move the frontmost window of any application. Needs the Accessibility permission, which Caduceus asks for once and never prompts for again.

items.name: Window: left half
items.detail: Fills the left half of the display the window is currently on, stopping at the menu bar and the Dock rather than sliding under them.

items.name: Window: right half
items.detail: Fills the right half of the current display. Pairs exactly with the left half — no gap, no overlap.

items.name: Window: top half
items.detail: Fills the upper half of the current display.

items.name: Window: bottom half
items.detail: Fills the lower half of the current display.

items.name: Window: top-left quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: top-right quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: bottom-left quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: bottom-right quarter
items.detail: One of four quarters that tile the usable screen area exactly.

items.name: Window: first third
items.detail: The left third of the display. Thirds are computed to add up exactly, so three windows leave no seam.

items.name: Window: middle third
items.detail: The middle third of the display.

items.name: Window: last third
items.detail: The right third of the display.

items.name: Window: first two-thirds
items.detail: The left two-thirds — the wide half of a two-thirds/one-third split.

items.name: Window: last two-thirds
items.detail: The right two-thirds.

items.name: Window: maximize
items.detail: Fills the whole usable area of the display. Not macOS full screen — the window keeps its title bar and stays in the current Space.

items.name: Window: almost maximize
items.detail: 92% of the display, centred — large without hiding what is behind it.

items.name: Window: reasonable size
items.detail: Two-thirds of the display, centred. The size to put a window back to after it has been dragged somewhere odd.

items.name: Window: center
items.detail: Centres the window without changing its size — a move, not a resize.

items.name: Window: make bigger
items.detail: Grows the window by 10% around its own centre, stopping at the edges of the display.

items.name: Window: make smaller
items.detail: Shrinks the window by 10% around its own centre, stopping before it becomes too small to use.

items.name: Window: move to next display
items.detail: Moves the window to the next display, keeping where it sat proportionally — so a window in the top-right corner arrives in the top-right corner, whatever size the other screen is.

items.name: Window: move to previous display
items.detail: The same, in the other direction.

items.name: Window: center half
items.detail: Half the width and half the height, centred — the size to read something in without it filling the screen.

items.name: Window: top third
items.detail: The upper third of the display, full width. Thirds by row rather than by column.

items.name: Window: bottom third
items.detail: The lower third of the display, full width.

items.name: Window: top two-thirds
items.detail: The upper two-thirds, full width — pairs with the bottom third.

items.name: Window: bottom two-thirds
items.detail: The lower two-thirds, full width.

items.name: Window: center two-thirds
items.detail: Two-thirds of the height, full width, centred vertically.

items.name: Window: top-left sixth
items.detail: One cell of a two-row, three-column grid. Six windows tile the screen exactly.

items.name: Window: top-center sixth
items.detail: The top-middle cell of the six-way grid.

items.name: Window: top-right sixth
items.detail: The top-right cell of the six-way grid.

items.name: Window: bottom-left sixth
items.detail: The bottom-left cell of the six-way grid.

items.name: Window: bottom-center sixth
items.detail: The bottom-middle cell of the six-way grid.

items.name: Window: bottom-right sixth
items.detail: The bottom-right cell of the six-way grid.

items.name: Window: first fourth
items.detail: The leftmost quarter-width column. Four of these tile an ultrawide exactly.

items.name: Window: second fourth
items.detail: The second quarter-width column from the left.

items.name: Window: third fourth
items.detail: The third quarter-width column from the left.

items.name: Window: last fourth
items.detail: The rightmost quarter-width column.

items.name: Window: first three-fourths
items.detail: The left three-quarters — the wide side of a three-quarter/one-quarter split.

items.name: Window: last three-fourths
items.detail: The right three-quarters.

items.name: Window: bottom three-fourths
items.detail: The lower three-quarters, full width.

items.name: Window: center three-fourths

commandGroups.title: System
commandGroups.blurb: macOS settings, the Finder, power and the session — driven by the tools macOS already ships, so none of it needs anything installed.

items.name: Force quit something
items.detail: Every running process, sorted by what is actually costing you, refreshed as you watch. Stop sends SIGTERM so a program can save first; Force is a second, separate choice.

items.name: Toggle dark mode
items.detail: Switches macOS between light and dark appearance. Needs permission to control System Events, which macOS asks for the first time.

items.name: Toggle Stage Manager
items.detail: Turns Stage Manager on or off and restarts the window manager so the change takes effect immediately.

items.name: Toggle hidden files in Finder
items.detail: Shows or hides dotfiles, then restarts Finder.

items.name: Toggle desktop icons
items.detail: Hides everything on the desktop, or brings it back. Nothing is moved or deleted — Finder just stops drawing it.

items.name: Restart Finder
items.detail: Relaunches Finder. The usual fix when a mounted volume will not go away.

items.name: Restart the Dock
items.detail: Relaunches the Dock, which also resets Mission Control and Stage Manager.

items.name: Restart the menu bar
items.detail: Relaunches SystemUIServer, which redraws the menu bar extras when one gets stuck.

items.name: Lock the screen
items.detail: Locks immediately, the same as the Apple menu's Lock Screen — regardless of the password delay set for sleep.

items.name: Turn the display off
items.detail: Puts the display to sleep without sleeping the machine, so anything running keeps running.

items.name: Sleep
items.detail: Puts the Mac to sleep.

items.name: Start the screen saver
items.detail: Starts the screen saver straight away.

items.name: Log out
items.detail: Ends the session. Applications are asked to save first, as they would be from the Apple menu.

items.name: Restart
items.detail: Restarts the Mac.

items.name: Shut down
items.detail: Shuts the Mac down.

items.name: Toggle Bluetooth
items.detail: Turns Bluetooth on or off. Uses blueutil when it is installed; otherwise it drives the Control Centre item, which needs the Accessibility permission.

items.name: Show the desktop
items.detail: Sends the Show Desktop key, sweeping every window aside. Sending it again brings them back.

items.name: Hide all apps except the frontmost
items.detail: Sends ⌥⌘H, so macOS's own rules about what can be hidden still apply.

items.name: Unhide all hidden apps
items.detail: Brings every hidden application back on screen, and says how many there were.

items.name: Quit all apps
items.detail: Asks every visible application to quit, so anything with unsaved work still prompts. Caduceus and Finder are left alone.

items.name: Quit all apps except the frontmost
items.detail: The same, sparing whatever you are currently working in. Caduceus and Finder are left alone.

items.name: Open the camera
items.detail: Opens Photo Booth, which is the camera app every Mac ships with.

items.name: Brightness up
items.detail: Raises display brightness by synthesising the hardware key, which is the only route Apple has not broken. Needs the Accessibility permission.

items.name: Brightness down
items.detail: Lowers display brightness. Needs the Accessibility permission.

items.name: Emoji and symbols
items.detail: Opens macOS's own emoji and symbol picker, which inserts straight into whatever you were typing in.

items.name: Open the camera
items.detail: Photo Booth, for when you need to check what the camera can see.

items.name: Quit every app except this one
items.detail: Asks each app to quit, so anything with unsaved work gets to put its dialog up rather than losing it. Finder and Caduceus are left alone.

commandGroups.title: Sound & media

items.name: Volume up
items.detail: Raises the output volume by 10% and unmutes, the way the hardware key does.

items.name: Volume down
items.detail: Lowers the output volume by 10%.

items.name: Mute / unmute
items.detail: Toggles output mute and says which state it landed in.

items.name: Set volume to 0%
items.detail: Silences the output by setting the level to zero, which is different from muting — the slider moves, so the next volume-up starts from silence.

items.name: Set volume to 25%
items.detail: Sets the output level to a quarter and releases mute.

items.name: Set volume to 50%
items.detail: Sets the output level to half and releases mute.

items.name: Set volume to 75%
items.detail: Sets the output level to three-quarters and releases mute.

items.name: Set volume to 100%
items.detail: Sets the output level to maximum and releases mute.

items.name: Change the sound output
items.detail: Every connected output device, with the current one marked. Switching is immediate and system-wide. Devices are tracked by their CoreAudio UID, which survives a reboot — unlike the numeric id macOS reassigns freely.

items.name: Change the microphone
items.detail: Every connected input device, with the current one marked.

items.name: Play / pause
items.detail: Plays or pauses whichever of Music or Spotify is actually running, preferring the one already playing.

items.name: Next track
items.detail: Skips forward and shows what started.

items.name: Previous track
items.detail: Goes back a track.

items.name: What is playing

items.name: Mute
items.detail: Sets the system volume to zero. Running it again puts it back where it was.

items.name: Spotify: play or pause
items.detail: Toggles playback without switching to Spotify. Needs Automation permission for Spotify, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Spotify: next track
items.detail: Skips forward. Needs Automation permission for Spotify, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Spotify: previous track
items.detail: Back one track. Needs Automation permission for Spotify, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Spotify: what is playing

items.name: Spotify: copy a link to this track

items.name: Spotify: toggle shuffle
items.detail: Turns shuffle on or off. Needs Automation permission for Spotify, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Spotify: toggle repeat
items.detail: Turns repeat on or off. Needs Automation permission for Spotify, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Spotify: louder
items.detail: Raises Spotify's own volume by ten, without touching the system volume. Needs Automation permission for Spotify, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Spotify: quieter
items.detail: Lowers Spotify's own volume by ten. Needs Automation permission for Spotify, which macOS asks for once.

commandGroups.title: Screen & text
commandGroups.blurb: Capture the screen and read text off it. Recognition runs on-device through Apple's Vision framework; no image leaves the machine.

items.name: Record the screen
items.detail: Screen video with the audio your Mac is playing — the thing ⇧⌘5 cannot do without an audio driver. Your microphone goes on its own track. Needs macOS 13 and the Screen Recording permission.

items.name: Copy text from the screen
items.detail: Drag a box over anything on screen — a screenshot, a video still, an error dialog — and the text inside it is recognised and copied. Recognition runs on-device through Apple's Vision framework, and the capture is deleted as soon as it has been read.

items.name: Read text from the selected image
items.detail: The same recognition, run over the image files selected in Finder.

commandGroups.title: Developer tools
commandGroups.blurb: Encoders, hashes, identifiers, formatters and inspectors. Every one of these runs locally, which is the point — a JWT or an API payload should never be pasted into a website to be read.

items.name: Regex tester
items.detail: Tests a pattern against sample text, shows every match with its capture groups and positions, and explains the pattern in plain English one token at a time. Runs on this Mac — nothing is sent anywhere.

items.name: Cron parser
items.detail: Reads a standard five-field cron expression, describes it in plain English, and lists its next several run times in this Mac's own time zone — including the day-of-month/day-of-week quirk that makes a schedule look stricter than it runs.

items.name: cURL / HTTP playground
items.detail: Paste a curl command — including whatever a browser’s “Copy as cURL” produces — and it is parsed, shown back, and replayed for real. –k/--insecure is recorded but never honoured: TLS is always verified regardless of what the pasted command asked for.

items.name: Generate a UUID
items.detail: A random version-4 UUID, copied as soon as it appears.

items.name: Generate ten UUIDs
items.detail: Ten version-4 UUIDs, one per line, for seeding fixtures.

items.name: Generate a ULID
items.detail: A ULID: a 48-bit millisecond timestamp followed by 80 random bits, in Crockford base32. Sorts by creation time, which is why you would use one instead of a UUID as a database key.

items.name: Generate a Nano ID
items.detail: A 21-character URL-safe identifier — shorter than a UUID and safe to put in a path.

items.name: Generate a password
items.detail: 24 characters from the system's cryptographic random source, guaranteed to contain every character class. Leaves out l, I, O, 0 and 1, because a password nobody can read off a screen gets written down somewhere worse.

items.name: Base64 encode  ·  base64 …
items.detail: Encodes what you type to standard base64, with padding.

items.name: Base64 decode  ·  unbase64 …
items.detail: Decodes base64 back to text. Tolerates missing padding, embedded newlines and either alphabet, because pasted tokens rarely arrive clean.

items.name: Base64 encode (URL-safe)
items.detail: The URL-safe alphabet with no padding — what JWTs and data URLs use.

items.name: Base64 decode (URL-safe)
items.detail: Decodes the URL-safe alphabet back to text.

items.name: Hex encode  ·  hex …
items.detail: Each byte of the input as two lowercase hex digits.

items.name: Hex decode  ·  unhex …
items.detail: Hex back to text. Accepts `0x` prefixes and colon- or dash-separated bytes.

items.name: URL encode  ·  urlencode …
items.detail: Percent-encodes everything outside the unreserved set, so the result is safe anywhere in a URL.

items.name: URL decode  ·  urldecode …
items.detail: Reverses percent-encoding, and reads `+` as a space the way a query string means it.

items.name: HTML escape  ·  htmlescape …
items.detail: Escapes the five characters that change the meaning of markup.

items.name: HTML unescape
items.detail: Turns entities back into characters, resolving `&` last so `&lt;` comes back as `<` rather than `<`.

items.name: Decode a JWT  ·  jwt …
items.detail: Shows a token's header and payload, formatted, and says whether it has expired. The signature is *not* verified — that needs the key, and a tool that showed a tick without one would be worse than none. Nothing is sent anywhere.

items.name: Format JSON  ·  json …
items.detail: Pretty-prints JSON with two-space indentation, and names the parse error if it is not valid.

items.name: Minify JSON
items.detail: Strips every byte of whitespace and reports how many that saved.

items.name: Escape as a JSON string
items.detail: Wraps the input in quotes and escapes it, ready to paste into a JSON document.

items.name: Current timestamp
items.detail: The Unix time now, in seconds and milliseconds, with the ISO 8601 form alongside.

items.name: Convert a timestamp  ·  epoch …
items.detail: Reads an epoch number or a date and shows the other. Ten digits are treated as seconds and thirteen as milliseconds, which stays unambiguous until the year 2286.

items.name: Convert a colour  ·  color …
items.detail: Reads a colour in any notation people paste and shows hex, RGB and HSL — plus the WCAG contrast against white and black, so you know which one the text can be.

items.name: Convert number bases  ·  base …
items.detail: Shows one number in decimal, hex, octal and binary at once. Reads `0x`, `0b` and `0o` prefixes.

items.name: Random number  ·  random …
items.detail: A number in a range you give — `5-10`, `5 10` or a bare `100` meaning 1 to 100.

items.name: SHA-256 hash  ·  sha256 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with SHA-256 and copies the digest.

items.name: SHA-512 hash  ·  sha512 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with SHA-512.

items.name: SHA-1 hash  ·  sha1 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with SHA-1. Broken for signatures; still what git object ids use.

items.name: MD5 hash  ·  md5 …
items.detail: Hashes the input with MD5. Fine for checking a download, never for a password.

items.name: Format YAML  ·  yaml …
items.detail: Pretty-prints the block and flow YAML people actually write — comments and multi-document ‘---’ streams included. Anchors, aliases, explicit tags and merge keys are reported as errors rather than silently reshaped.

items.name: Validate YAML
items.detail: Checks whether text is valid YAML without changing it, under the same rules as the formatter — anchors, aliases and merge keys are refused rather than guessed at.

items.name: Format XML  ·  xml …
items.detail: Checks well-formedness the way a browser's parser would — matching tags, quoted attributes, exactly one root, no bare & or < — and pretty-prints what parses. Not DTD or schema validation, since neither is fetched.

items.name: Validate XML
items.detail: Checks whether markup is well-formed XML, without changing it.

items.name: HTML entity encode  ·  htmlentity …
items.detail: The wide version: escapes the five markup-significant characters by name and every other non-ASCII character as a numeric reference — not just the five “HTML escape” covers.

items.name: HTML entity decode  ·  unhtmlentity …
items.detail: Decodes the classic named HTML entity set (©, —, ½, Greek letters and more) plus decimal and hex numeric references back to text. An entity missing its ‘;’, or naming something unknown, is left exactly as written.

items.name: Format SQL  ·  sql …
items.detail: Breaks a query onto readable lines: one major clause per line, joins and boolean conjunctions indented beneath, keywords uppercased, strings and identifiers left alone. A line-breaker, not a full parser — it works across dialects rather than getting one exactly right.

commandGroups.title: Text
commandGroups.blurb: Reshape whatever you type or paste: case, line order, counts and cleanup.

items.name: Summarise
items.detail: Boils the text down to its point. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Rewrite: professional
items.detail: Same meaning, work register. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Rewrite: friendly
items.detail: Same meaning, warmer. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Rewrite: concise
items.detail: Same meaning, fewer words. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Rewrite: diplomatic
items.detail: Same meaning, less edge. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Fix grammar and style
items.detail: Typos, run-ons and passive voice. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Explain simply
items.detail: Jargon turned into plain language. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Draft a polite reply
items.detail: Reads it and writes the answer. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Bullet-point it
items.detail: A paragraph becomes three or four lines. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Suggest a title
items.detail: Headlines and subject lines. Runs against whichever AI backend you configured — a local model or your own key — and puts the result on the clipboard.

items.name: Text expander
items.detail: Snippets with placeholders that fill themselves in — today’s date, next week’s, whatever is on the clipboard — plus emoji searched by meaning rather than name, Markdown pasted as styled text, and a proofreader for what a spellchecker cannot see.

items.name: Lorem ipsum
items.detail: Three sentences of placeholder text.

items.name: Slugify  ·  slug …
items.detail: Lowercases and dashes the input into something safe for a URL, keeping accented letters intact.

items.name: Count words and characters  ·  count …
items.detail: Words, characters, lines, paragraphs, sentences and an estimated reading time.

items.name: Sort lines A→Z  ·  sort …
items.detail: Sorts the lines you paste, ignoring case.

items.name: Sort lines Z→A
items.detail: The same, reversed.

items.name: Remove duplicate lines  ·  dedupe …
items.detail: Keeps the first occurrence of each line and says how many went.

items.name: Reverse line order
items.detail: Last line first.

items.name: Shuffle lines
items.detail: Randomises line order with a Fisher-Yates shuffle over the system random source.

items.name: Number lines
items.detail: Prefixes each line with `1.`, `2.` and so on.

items.name: Join lines
items.detail: Collapses lines into one comma-separated line, dropping blanks.

items.name: Trim whitespace
items.detail: Removes leading and trailing whitespace from every line.

items.name: Count repeated lines
items.detail: How often each line appears, most frequent first — a `sort | uniq -c` you do not have to remember.

items.name: Change case: UPPER CASE  ·  upper …
items.detail: Everything uppercased. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: lower case  ·  lower …
items.detail: Everything lowercased. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: Title Case  ·  title …
items.detail: Each word capitalised, punctuation and spacing untouched. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: Sentence case  ·  sentence …
items.detail: Capitalises the first letter after every sentence terminator. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: snake_case  ·  snake …
items.detail: Words joined with underscores. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: kebab-case  ·  kebab …
items.detail: Words joined with dashes. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: camelCase  ·  camel …
items.detail: First word lowercase, the rest capitalised and joined. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

items.name: Change case: PascalCase  ·  pascal …
items.detail: Every word capitalised and joined. Handles camelCase humps, so an identifier converts the way you meant.

commandGroups.title: Files & Finder
commandGroups.blurb: Actions on the current Finder selection. Deletion always means the Trash, never an unrecoverable remove.

items.name: Free up disk space
items.detail: What is taking your disk, and getting it back. Caches, logs, build intermediates and the leftovers of apps you removed — measured, explained one by one, and moved to the Trash rather than deleted. Also uninstalls an app properly, with everything it scattered through your Library.

items.name: Tidy a folder
items.detail: Files a messy Desktop (or any folder) into subfolders by what things are, when they were changed, or how big they are. Shows you the plan first and moves nothing until you say so — and Undo puts every file back.

items.name: Arrange desktop icons into a shape
items.detail: Lays the icons on your Desktop out in a circle, a heart, a spiral, an even grid or a single line, scaled to fit your screen between the menu bar and the Dock. Shows the arrangement before it happens, and Undo puts every icon back exactly where it was. Needs Automation permission for Finder, and Finder's own Sort By has to be set to None — this says so if it is not.

items.name: Empty the Trash
items.detail: Empties the Trash through Finder, so the usual warnings about locked items still apply.

items.name: Open the Trash
items.detail: Opens the Trash in Finder and brings Finder forward.

items.name: Find a file
items.detail: Searches file names through Spotlight, so it answers from an index that already exists rather than walking the disk. Choosing a result reveals it in Finder.

items.name: Largest files
items.detail: The biggest files in your home folder, over 100 MB, newest measurement first. Also answered from the Spotlight index, so it returns immediately instead of spinning the disk. Choosing one reveals it in Finder.

items.name: Compress the Finder selection
items.detail: Zips what is selected in Finder into an archive beside it, using the same tool Finder's own Compress uses — so resource forks and extended attributes survive. Never overwrites an existing archive.

items.name: Expand the selected archive
items.detail: Unpacks the selected archives into folders beside them.

items.name: Move the Finder selection to the Trash
items.detail: Deletes through Finder, so it lands in the Trash and Cmd-Z puts it back.

items.name: Quick Look the Finder selection
items.detail: Opens the macOS preview panel for what is selected, without switching to Finder.

items.name: Open the Finder selection in Terminal
items.detail: Opens Terminal at the selected folder, or at the folder containing the selected file.

items.name: Copy the path of the Finder selection
items.detail: Copies the POSIX path of everything selected, one per line.

items.name: Open the latest download
items.detail: Opens the newest file in ~/Downloads, skipping the part-files browsers leave behind mid-download.

items.name: Copy the path of the latest download
items.detail: The same file, as a path on the clipboard.

items.name: Open the Trash
items.detail: Shows what is in it, before you empty it.

items.name: Empty the Trash
items.detail: Deletes everything in it. There is no undo for this one, which is why it asks first.

items.name: View /etc/hosts
items.detail: Every alias entry in /etc/hosts, this machine's local overrides for name resolution. Read-only — editing needs root, which this never asks for.

items.name: Toggle Wi-Fi
items.detail: Turns Wi-Fi on or off on whichever interface is actually the Wi-Fi one — not a hardcoded en0.

items.name: Local IP addresses
items.detail: Every interface that has an address, labelled the way Network settings labels it, plus the default router.

items.name: Public IP address
items.detail: This machine's address as the internet sees it. The one command in Caduceus that deliberately leaves the machine — it runs only when you pick this row.

items.name: Wi-Fi details
items.detail: The network you are on, the address it gave you, the router and the interface name.

items.name: Look up a hostname  ·  dns …
items.detail: Resolves a hostname to its addresses using the system resolver.

items.name: Ping a host  ·  ping …
items.detail: Five packets, summarised as loss and round-trip time.

commandGroups.title: Developer environment
commandGroups.blurb: What is running on this machine: ports, repositories, SSH hosts and containers.

items.name: Git commit assist
items.detail: Reads a repository’s status and diff and drafts a commit message through whichever AI backend is configured. Every git call is read-only — this never stages or commits; you still press commit yourself.

items.name: Dependency inspector
items.detail: Reads a package.json, Cargo.toml, or requirements.txt and shows how tightly each dependency is pinned — exact, a movable range, or unpinned entirely. No network lookups: only what the manifest itself says.

items.name: Listening ports
items.detail: Every process holding a TCP port open, with its pid. Choosing one stops it with SIGTERM, so a dev server flushes its logs and removes its socket rather than being killed outright. Type a number after the keyword to narrow to one port.

items.name: Git repositories
items.detail: Repositories under the usual project folders — Developer, Projects, Code, src, dev, repos and Documents/GitHub — with the branch each one is on. Choosing one opens it in Terminal. Only two levels deep, so it stays instant.

items.name: SSH hosts
items.detail: The hosts defined in ~/.ssh/config, with their hostname and user. Choosing one opens Terminal and connects. Wildcard patterns are skipped, because they are rules rather than machines you can reach.

items.name: Docker containers
items.detail: Every container, running or not, with its image and status. Choosing one starts or stops it. Says plainly whether Docker is missing or simply not running.

commandGroups.title: Utilities
commandGroups.blurb: The small things that are faster to type than to go and find.

items.name: Sticky notes
items.detail: Somewhere to put four words before you lose them. Saves as you type, survives a restart, and never asks you to name a file.

items.name: Ask about part of my screen
items.detail: Drag a box around anything — a stack trace, an error dialog, a chart — and ask about it. The text is read on this Mac by Apple’s own Vision framework; only that text reaches the model, never the picture.

items.name: Ask about this window
items.detail: Reads the frontmost window instead of asking you to drag a box. Same on-device OCR; the same rule that only the text leaves your Mac.

items.name: Summarise a web page
items.detail: Fetches a URL, strips the navigation and the adverts, and summarises what is left. The page is fetched by Caduceus, not by a model — nothing about you goes with the request.

items.name: Add a calendar event
items.detail: “Lunch with Mark next Tuesday at 12:30pm” becomes a real Apple Calendar event. The date is parsed on this Mac, not by a model, so it works offline and answers instantly — and refuses rather than guessing when it cannot read what you meant.

items.name: What is on today
items.detail: Today’s remaining calendar events, read straight from Apple Calendar. Does not launch Calendar to look.

items.name: Search my files by meaning
items.detail: Finds a document by what it is about rather than what it is called — “the note where I worked out the database schema”. The index is built and searched entirely on this Mac; if a local model is running it is used to understand meaning, and if not the search still works on words alone.

items.name: Read a document or page
items.detail: Summarise a PDF or ask it a question, or paste a URL and get the article without the adverts. Long documents are read in sections and the answer says when it only covered part of one.

items.name: Image tools
items.detail: Compress and convert, resize to a preset, strip EXIF and GPS before sharing a photo, and find duplicates in a folder. Originals are never overwritten — every result is written beside the file it came from.

items.name: Add a widget
items.detail: Pins a small always-on-top panel above every app and every Space — a clock, a crypto or stock ticker, a sports scoreboard, or a Kalshi/Polymarket board. Drag it anywhere; it remembers its spot across restarts.

items.name: Privacy and security
items.detail: A passphrase generator, a clipboard that clears itself, a microphone mute, a log of which apps recently used the camera or microphone, and a file vault. The vault uses Argon2id — a forgotten passphrase means the file is gone, and it says so before you encrypt anything.

items.name: Time management
items.detail: A world clock for a handful of zones side by side, a converter for “5pm EST in Tokyo”, named countdown timers, a stopwatch with laps, and a pomodoro cycle. The counting happens in Caduceus itself, so a timer keeps running — and still notifies you — after this window is closed.

items.name: QR code
items.detail: Turns a link or a line of text into a QR code, so a phone can pick it up off the screen. Starts from whatever the frontmost browser tab is showing. Encoded on this Mac — nothing is uploaded to draw it.

items.name: Colors
items.detail: Pick a colour from anywhere on screen, or type any notation, and get every other notation, its name, its tints and shades, what goes with it, and whether text on it passes WCAG. Pull a palette out of an image too.

items.name: Convert units
items.detail: Length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, time, data, pressure, energy and angle — all offline arithmetic on definitions. Currency too, which is the one thing here that needs the internet and says so.

items.name: Meeting notes
items.detail: Records both sides of a call — the room through system audio, you through the microphone — transcribes on-device as it goes, and keeps your notes beside the transcript. Nothing is uploaded and no bot joins the meeting.

items.name: Cite this page
items.detail: Reads whatever your browser has in front and writes the citation in MLA, APA, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver and BibTeX at once. Fills in the author and date from the page when you ask it to, and admits when it cannot rather than inventing one.

items.name: Eject all disks
items.detail: Ejects every removable volume under /Volumes, and says which ones refused.

items.name: Keep this Mac awake  ·  awake …
items.detail: Opens the Keep Awake page: sessions that run indefinitely, for a duration, or until a time, with a live countdown — everything Amphetamine's core does, on the caffeinate macOS already ships. Or skip the page: `awake 45` and `awake 2h` start a timed session straight from here. Sessions are tied to Caduceus's process, so quitting the app always re-enables sleep.

items.name: Allow this Mac to sleep
items.detail: Ends the running keep-awake session immediately.

items.name: Define a word  ·  define …
items.detail: Looks a word up in the Dictionary app that ships with macOS. No network involved.

items.name: About this Mac
items.detail: Model, chip, cores, memory, macOS version, battery and uptime, on one screen and ready to paste into a bug report.

items.name: Check Caduceus's permissions
items.detail: See Accessibility and Screen Recording status, open the right Settings panes, and repair stale grants after an update.

items.name: Clipboard history
items.detail: Everything you have copied — text, images, file paths — searchable and pinnable, kept in a local database that never leaves this Mac. The /v prefix filters it directly.

items.name: System monitor
items.detail: Live CPU, memory, disk and network, with the processes using them — and a way to end one that has stopped behaving.

items.name: Open the Manage window  ·  manage …
items.detail: The tabbed window for everything with live state: keep-awake sessions, sound devices, listening ports, Docker containers and this Mac's details. Tabs stay open while you use another, like a browser — ⌘1–⌘5 switch, ⌘W closes.

items.name: Chrome: new tab
items.detail: Opens a tab in the front window. Needs Automation permission for Google Chrome, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Chrome: new window
items.detail: A fresh window. Needs Automation permission for Google Chrome, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Chrome: new incognito window
items.detail: A window that keeps no history. Needs Automation permission for Google Chrome, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Chrome: copy this page's address
items.detail: The URL of the tab in front. Needs Automation permission for Google Chrome, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Chrome: copy this page's title
items.detail: The title of the tab in front. Needs Automation permission for Google Chrome, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Chrome: copy every open tab
items.detail: Title and address of every tab in the front window, one per line. Needs Automation permission for Google Chrome, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Safari: copy this page's address
items.detail: The URL of the tab in front. Needs Automation permission for Safari, which macOS asks for once.

items.name: Run an Apple Shortcut  ·  shortcut …
items.detail: Runs any shortcut from the Shortcuts app by name, with optional text as its input. Everything you have already built in Shortcuts is reachable from the search bar.

items.name: List your Apple Shortcuts
items.detail: Every shortcut the Shortcuts app knows about, so you can see what is runnable.
